3.text: villages (both Chukchee and Eskimo), and also between Asia and America

10.text: In the tale of “Elendi and his Sons,” the hero, coming to an American

11.text: Eskimo, requests “a score of ground-seal skins, a score each of bleached and

12.text: black-dyed coils of thong, the same of rough-seal skins; whatever you have,

13.text: one score of each.” The host asks for an equivalent, but Elendi has nothing:

14.text: so a quarrel arises, and they fight. Elendi vanquishes the Eskimo, commands

15.text: the people of the village to deliver up to him everything he had asked for,

16.text: and returns home carrying his subdued enemy away as a slave.¹
